input.verdict: Weak support: Sb-rich films should be a mix of AgSbO3 and Sb6O13. MEGNet puts the Sb6O13 gap at about 2.05 eV, close to the 2.1 eV photons, so it may form a heterojunction with the absorbing AgSbO3. The other AgSbO3 polymorph has a small gap (0.63 eV), which makes the phase picture at 1:1 uncertain. Measuring index 11 (Ag 0.29) covers the Sb-rich half of the line.

input.verdict: Against the Sb-rich side and mildly for Ag-rich: Ag7Sb9O25 (Ag 0.44) is above the hull (0.039 eV/atom) and has a small gap, so the Sb-rich side offers no better absorber. That fits index 11 measuring about 10x lower than index 5. Moving slightly Ag-rich of 1:1 (index 3, Ag 0.567) keeps AgSbO3 as the main phase with some Ag3SbO4, which may improve absorption and conductivity.

content.text:
I've submitted **index 5 (Ag 0.504 / Sb 0.496)** as the best composition. Its EQE was 0.064%, the highest of the three merit measurements I was allowed.

| Index | Ag fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | 0.504 | 0.0638 |
| 3 | 0.567 | 0.0573 |
| 11 | 0.291 | 0.0056 |

- **Why 1:1 first:** the models pointed to AgSbO₃. MACE puts it on the stability hull, and MEGNet predicts a band gap of about 1.78 eV. That is below the 2.1 eV light, so it should absorb.
- **Sb-rich side:** index 11 came in about 10x lower. That fits Sb oxides having predicted gaps near or above 2.05 eV, so they absorb poorly at this photon energy.
- **Ag-rich side:** index 3 was a little lower than index 5. Further toward Ag you approach Ag₃SbO₄, which is predicted to be nearly metallic (0.09 eV gap), so I didn't expect a better result there.

The peak looks to be near 1:1, but with three points that is a judgement, not a confirmed maximum. I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements, so which phases are actually present in the films is inferred from the models, not measured.
